chunks: Al-Ḥalabī narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he was asked about a man who led a people in prayer, prayed one rakʿah with them, then died. He said:

“They should appoint another man, who will count that rakʿah, and they should place the deceased behind them. Whoever touched him must perform ghusl (ritual bath). And whoever led a people in prayer while he was junub or without wudu (ablution), then repetition is upon him, while it is not upon them to repeat, and it is not upon him to inform them; and if that had been obligatory upon him, he would have perished.”
He said: I said, “How was he to deal with one who had gone out to Khurāsān, and how was he to deal with one whom he did not know?” He said: “This is lifted from him.”

key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: Repetition of the prayer due to invalidity on the part of the Imam.
key_terms.الْمَيِّتَ: The deceased person, here referring to the Imam who died during the prayer.
key_terms.جُنُبٌ: In a state of janabah, major ritual impurity requiring ghusl.
key_terms.رَكْعَةً: A unit of salat (prayer) already completed and counted in the congregational prayer.
key_terms.مَوْضُوعٌ: Lifted or removed from him, meaning not required or not binding in that case.
key_terms.وُضُوءٍ: Wudu (ablution), the minor ritual purification required for salat (prayer).
key_terms.يَغْتَسِلُ: He performs ghusl (ritual bath), here due to touching the dead body.

ai.seo_question: What happens if the Imam dies during congregational prayer or led the prayer without wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives fiqh rulings related to congregational salat (prayer) when the Imam dies during the prayer and when an Imam leads while in janabah or without wudu (ablution). It establishes that the congregation may continue behind a replacement leader, that the invalidity returns to the Imam himself in the latter case, and that informing all followers is not required when doing so would be practically impossible.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.1198 - Al-Halabi narrated from Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) that he was asked about a man who led a congregation, prayed one rak'ah with them, and then passed away.
Imam (as) said: "They should appoint another man to lead them, count the rak'ah (already prayed), and move the deceased to the back. Those who touched him must perform ghusl (ritual purification).

If someone led a congregation while in a state of major ritual impurity (janabah) or without wudu', they must repeat their prayer, but the congregation does not need to repeat theirs, and the Imam is not obligated to inform them. If he had to inform them, it would cause great distress."

I asked: "How would this apply to someone who went to Khurasan or to those who are unknown?"
Imam (as) replied: "This is not applicable to him (in such a case)."
